title: Scheme composition coherence of normalized rational pullback
statement: Let $\ell$ be prime, $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ finite, $A=\mathcal O_E$ and $\varpi$ a uniformizer [def-weil-l-adic-coefficient-extension]. Let $X$ be a noetherian finite-dimensional scheme with $\ell$ invertible. On its small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site] put $B_X=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}(A/\varpi^n)_X$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-coefficient-datum] and $E_X=B_X[1/\varpi]$. Module sheaves, sheaf tensor products, derived categories and cohomology are as in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-derived-cohomology-sheaves]. Write $\mathcal C_X=D^b_c(X,A)$ for the completed integral category including compatible etale-origin witnesses [def-weil-pbc-bounded-constructible-complete], and $Q:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal R_X=\mathcal C_X[1/\varpi]$ for its raw rationalization [def-weil-pbc-rational-category]. A rational module sheaf is constructible when on a finite locally closed stratification it is pro-etale locally finite free [def-constructible-stratification, def-weil-pbc-continuous-constructible-module]. Write $F_X(K)=E_X\otimes^L_{B_X}K$ and $J_X(QK)=F_X(K)$, $J_X(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_X(f)$ for the functor specified in [lem-per-rational-module-realization-functor]. For each $g:X'\to X$ between schemes with the same hypotheses, write $P_g$ for ordinary integral derived module pullback, $\widehat P_g$ for [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback], $G_g=E_{X'}\otimes^L_{g^{-1}E_X}g^{-1}(-)$, and $\alpha_g:J_{X'}Q\widehat P_g\xrightarrow{\sim}G_gJ_X$ for the specific comparison of [lem-per-rational-realization-pullback-comparison]. For $h:X''\to X'$ the two routes from $J_{X''}Q\widehat P_h\widehat P_gK$ to $G_{g\circ h}J_XQK$ agree: one uses the completed composition comparison and $\alpha_{g\circ h}$, the other uses $\alpha_h$, $G_h\alpha_g$ and the ambient composition comparison $G_hG_g\cong G_{g\circ h}$. The analogous identity diagram agrees with the ambient identity pullback. These are equations of natural transformations for the specified maps, not merely existence of isomorphic endpoints. The integral coefficient maps satisfy $c_{g\circ h}=c_h\circ h^{-1}c_g$ under inverse-image composition, as tested against every finite quotient. On K-flat representatives the ambient composition sends $e''\otimes e'\otimes k$ to $e''h^{-1}(e')\otimes k$ and its identity removes $1$; conjugation by the specified units $\gamma$ preserves these formulas and equations [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons, lem-weil-pbc-constant-completion-equivalence].

source.place: Remark 6.8.15, expanded identity/composition equations for the finite-quotient coefficient maps and tensor/completion-unit comparisons, p. 62

proof.text:
Write $d_{g,n}:g^{-1}(A/\varpi^n)_X\to(A/\varpi^n)_{X'}$ for the finite constant-coefficient map. The definition of pro-etale inverse image and the adjunction-compatible site composition identify $d_{g\circ h,n}$ with $d_{h,n}h^{-1}d_{g,n}$: their adjoints both pull a constant section $a$ back to that same $a$ on $X''\times_XU$. This also proves the identity case and compatibility with the quotient transitions. By the definition of $c_g$, for every $n$,
$$\pi_{X'',n}c_hh^{-1}c_g=d_{h,n}h^{-1}d_{g,n}h^{-1}g^{-1}\pi_{X,n}=\pi_{X'',n}c_{g\circ h}.$$
The projections of the actual limit sheaf $B_{X''}$ are jointly monic, so $c_{g\circ h}=c_hh^{-1}c_g$, under inverse-image composition. The same argument gives $c_{\mathrm{id}}=1$. No inverse image is commuted with an inverse limit.

source.place: Tag 03CB, lemma-composition-morphisms-sites; finite-quotient computation for the coefficient maps

proof.text:
Denote ordinary integral and rational composition by $a:P_hP_g\xrightarrow{\sim}P_{g\circ h}$ and $b:G_hG_g\xrightarrow{\sim}G_{g\circ h}$. Apply the ringed-derived monoidal comparisons to the ring maps from Step 1 and to their localizations. They are defined on flat-term K-flat representatives, and ordinary pullback preserves that class. The inverse-image/localization comparison is the specified one, preserves the unit, and satisfies its identity/composition equations. Let $\delta_g:F_{X'}P_g\xrightarrow{\sim}G_gF_X$ be balanced tensor flattening from the realization comparison. After these identifications both paths from $F_{X''}P_hP_gK$ to $G_{g\circ h}F_XK$ send the local generator $e''\otimes b'\otimes k$ to $e''\,\iota_{X''}(c_h(b'))\otimes k$, where $b'\in h^{-1}B_{X'}$ and $\iota_{X''}:B_{X''}\to E_{X''}$. Thus
$$\delta_{g\circ h}F_{X''}(a)=b\,G_h(\delta_g)\,\delta_{h,P_g}.$$
Equality holds on sheafified tensor complexes (the displayed balanced maps commute with restrictions and differentials), and hence on the derived functors. If $d_h:h^{-1}E_{X'}\to E_{X''}$ is the localized ring map, $b$ itself sends $e''\otimes e'\otimes k$ to $e''d_h(e')\otimes k$; its inverse inserts $1$. This is the formula in the statement, with $h^{-1}(e')$ acted on by $d_h$. Scalars have degree zero, so no sign is introduced.

source.place: Tags 0D6D (lemma-derived-pullback-composition), 07A4 (lemma-pullback-tensor-product); agent expansion of their balanced tensor formulas

proof.text: Let $\mathscr D_W^{\mathrm{comp}}\subset D(B_W)$ be the full locally derived $(\varpi)$-complete category, without a constructibility restriction. The Koszul completion reflector exists with its specified natural unit. The constant-to-completed coefficient equivalence identifies that unit with the finite-quotient tower unit. Consequently [def-weil-pbc-completed-pullback] identifies $\widehat P_g$ with completion of $P_g$, including $\gamma_g$, rather than just identifying their values. The ringed pushforward completion lemma says that $Rg_*$ preserves these full complete categories: its ideal hypothesis holds since Step 1 sends the constant scalar $\varpi$ to $\varpi$. Combining the reflector Hom bijection with the ordinary derived adjunction gives $\widehat P_g\dashv Rg_*$ on complete objects. The same applies to $h$ and $g\circ h$. This uses no isomorphism of the coefficient structure maps.

source.place: Tags 099J (lemma-pushforward-derived-complete), 0A0E (lemma-derived-completion-koszul), lemma-pushforward-derived-complete-adjoint; quotient-unit identification from proetale.tex Tags 099L, 099M

proof.text:
Use the reflected-compositor unit-normalization lemma on the three ambient categories $D(B_X),D(B_{X'}),D(B_{X''})$, their full complete subcategories of Step 3, and $L_{01}=P_g,L_{12}=P_h,L_{02}=P_{g\circ h}$. Take its right comparison to be the canonical derived direct-image composition comparison. The ordinary pullback comparison $a$ is its adjunction conjugate by the ringed-derived monoidal lemma. All the reflector and right-adjoint preservation hypotheses were verified in Step 3. The lemma therefore identifies the specified completed compositor $\widehat a:\widehat P_h\widehat P_g\to\widehat P_{g\circ h}$, defined by the restricted composite adjunction, and gives the equation
$$\widehat a_K\,\gamma_{h,\widehat P_gK}\,P_h(\gamma_{g,K})=\gamma_{g\circ h,K}\,a_K.$$
Since the quotient-tower construction has the same reflector and units, uniqueness in the reflector Hom bijection fixes this same compositor for that construction; no comparison is selected merely because its endpoints are isomorphic.

source.place: Tag 099N (lemma-pushforward-Noetherian-case), clause (2); agent expansion using the cited abstract reflector normalization

proof.text:
For $K\in\mathcal C_X$, the realization pullback comparison says $P_gK\in\mathcal C_{X'}$ and that the specified $\gamma_{g,K}$ is an isomorphism. Applying it also to $h$ and to $g\circ h$ makes every unit in Step 4 invertible; in particular $\widehat P_gK\in\mathcal C_{X'}$ since it is isomorphic to $P_gK$. Cancel the units in Step 4 to obtain
$$\widehat a_K=\gamma_{g\circ h,K}\,a_K\,P_h(\gamma_{g,K}^{-1})\,\gamma_{h,\widehat P_gK}^{-1}.$$
The comparison specified in the item is exactly $\alpha_g=\delta_g F_{X'}(\gamma_g^{-1})$, not a different natural isomorphism.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; algebraic cancellation using the specified comparison of the cited node

proof.text:
Abbreviate $F_{X''}$ to $F''$. Expand the second route using Step 5 and naturality of $\delta_h$ at $\gamma_g^{-1}:\widehat P_gK\to P_gK$:
$$\begin{aligned}
b\,G_h(\alpha_g)\,\alpha_{h,\widehat P_gK}
&=b\,G_h(\delta_g)\,\delta_{h,P_gK}\,F''(P_h\gamma_g^{-1})\,F''(\gamma_{h,\widehat P_gK}^{-1})\\
&=\delta_{g\circ h}\,F''(a_KP_h\gamma_g^{-1}\gamma_{h,\widehat P_gK}^{-1})\\
&=\delta_{g\circ h}\,F''(\gamma_{g\circ h,K}^{-1})\,F''(\widehat a_K)
=\alpha_{g\circ h,K}\,F''(\widehat a_K).
\end{aligned}$$
The second equality is precisely Step 2; the third is the unit equation of Step 4 with invertible units canceled. This proves the requested equality of the two specified transformations on integral representatives, including their naturality in $K$.

source.place: Remark 6.8.15; explicit naturality and cancellation calculation, agent supplied

proof.text:
Write $e:P_{\mathrm{id}}\to\mathrm{id}$ and $e_E:G_{\mathrm{id}}\to\mathrm{id}$ for the specified ambient identities. The reflector universal property says that the completed identity $\widehat e$ is characterized by $\widehat e_K\gamma_{\mathrm{id},K}=e_K$: both are the adjunction-compatible map to the already complete object $K$. Hence $\widehat e=e\gamma_{\mathrm{id}}^{-1}$. The identity case of balanced tensor flattening satisfies $e_E\delta_{\mathrm{id}}=F(e)$, since both maps multiply the coefficient into the module and remove the inserted $1$. Therefore
$$e_E\alpha_{\mathrm{id}}=F(e\gamma_{\mathrm{id}}^{-1})=F(\widehat e).$$
This is the identity diagram for the specified maps. It also shows that conjugation by $\gamma$ preserves the normalization of the identity, just as the equation of Step 4 does for composition.

source.place: Reflector universal property; identity specialization of sites-cohomology.tex Tags 0D6D and 07A4

proof.text: Finally $J_WQ=F_W$ with $J_W(f/\varpi^n)=\varpi^{-n}F_W(f)$. Every map used above is linear over the constant scalar $\varpi$: finite coefficient pullbacks fix that scalar, tensor flattening is balanced, and completion units are natural at scalar multiplication. Thus naturality for an integral map $f$ implies naturality for $f/\varpi^n$ by multiplying both sides by the same invertible scalar $\varpi^{-n}$. Every object of the raw rationalization is an integral object, so the equations of Steps 6 and 7 are equations of natural transformations on the entire raw rationalized categories. The ambient tensor formula in Step 2 is retained under these identifications; the completed maps are precisely its conjugates by the specified units, as computed in Step 5. No full-faithfulness assertion for $J$ is needed.
